questions.question: What's the difference between `permanent: true` and `permanent: false` in a redirects() entry?
options: There is no functional difference, only cosmetic
permanent: true emits a 308 status (browsers/crawlers update bookmarks and search results), permanent: false emits a 307 for a temporary move
permanent: false disables the redirect entirely
permanent: true only works in development mode
questions.explanation: The status code signals to browsers and search engines whether to treat the redirect as a lasting change (308, update references) or a temporary one (307, keep the original URL).

questions.question: How does a rewrite differ from a redirect from the visitor's point of view?
options: They behave identically in every way
With a rewrite, the URL bar still shows the original path even though a different destination actually serves the content
A rewrite always opens a new tab
A rewrite can only point to routes within the same app
questions.explanation: Unlike a redirect, a rewrite serves different content at the same visible URL — useful for transparently proxying another origin under your own domain.

questions.question: What does a Content-Security-Policy header help prevent?
options: An injected or malicious script from loading resources or executing freely, by restricting which origins scripts/styles/images may come from
Duplicate content in search engine results
questions.explanation: CSP limits what a script running on the page (including one injected via an XSS bug) is allowed to do, by whitelisting trusted origins for various resource types.

questions.question: Why do security headers and redirect rules belong in next.config.ts rather than duplicated inside individual route files?
options: Route files cannot set headers at all
They are cross-cutting concerns that should apply consistently across every route, including ones not yet written, from a single auditable place
It has no practical benefit, it's purely convention
next.config.ts is required for any routing to work
questions.explanation: Centralizing these rules avoids having to repeat them per-page and ensures new routes automatically inherit the same security posture.
